title: Germany's Gen Z Protests Draw Tens of Thousands, Then Turn Violent in Frankfurt and Other Cities
dek: Organizers say about 120,000 people joined rallies in 34 cities on Saturday. Nighttime looting, attacks on police and dozens of arrests followed, and the group distanced itself from the violence.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Frankfurt's Römer city hall, Paulsplatz entrance (historic public-domain file photo, not from the Oct. 31 protests)
image.credit: Carl Friedrich Fay, via Wikimedia Commons

keyPoints: Gen Z regelt ("Gen Z's Got This"), which organized the protests, said about 120,000 people joined rallies in 34 German cities on Saturday, the Washington Post reported.
Authorities in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin put the number at as many as 18,000 protesters in those cities, roughly half the organizers' estimate, the BBC reported.

Groups of people looted shops and smashed windows in downtown Frankfurt, and police reported injuries to dozens of officers, the Washington Post and CNN reported. Berlin police said 27 officers sustained minor injuries and almost 60 people were arrested, Euronews reported.
Gen Z regelt distanced itself from the violence. German officials have blamed infiltrators, CNN reported.
body:
Protests over affordability and education swept German cities on Saturday, organized by a movement called Gen Z regelt, loosely translated as "Gen Z's Got This." The rallies were largely peaceful for much of the day, but overnight violence in Frankfurt, Berlin and other cities led to shop looting and dozens of arrests.

## Turnout

The group said about 120,000 people took part in gatherings in 34 cities, the Washington Post reported. Police in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin reported as many as 18,000 protesters across those cities, roughly half the organizers' estimate, the BBC reported. The gap between the two figures is a reminder that the organizers' count has not been independently verified.

## Violence and arrests

After dark, people broke into shops in downtown Frankfurt, and windows were broken at a gun shop, CNN reported. Officers arrested a suspect and seized two weapons there. German news magazine Der Spiegel, cited by CNN, reported that more than 30 people were temporarily detained in Frankfurt.

In Berlin, police said almost 60 people were arrested and 27 officers sustained minor injuries, Euronews reported. Police in Leipzig used pepper spray after protests turned violent, and a police officer in Bonn was injured in a confrontation with a group, CNA reported. The Washington Post reported that dozens of police officers were injured in several cities.

Some reports put the total number of arrests above 200. Meridian has not been able to confirm a single official national tally in the sources reviewed for this story, so no overall arrest figure is given here.

## Demands and blame

The protests were about underfunded schools, cuts to education, social services, culture and healthcare, rising living costs and military conscription, according to Reuters Connect photo captions. Gen Z regelt distanced itself from the violence, the Washington Post reported. CNN reported that German officials blamed infiltrators for the unrest. Euronews reported that the protests were part of a wider youth-led wave across Europe, including the demonstrations in France on the same weekend.

Meridian will update this story as police publish official arrest and injury figures.
